messages:
tasha-design: Quick accessibility note from today's design review: Model Comparison tabs (Overview / Latency / Costs) are visually clear but keyboard focus outline is almost invisible in high-contrast mode. Also the selected tab state uses color only (blue underline), no aria-selected on the tablist. Screenshot: https://img.redwood/model-compare-tabs.png ben-frontend: I can see that. On Windows high-contrast the default outline becomes 1px; in our CSS we override outline-style but it's getting lost. Repro: open Model Compare, press Tab to focus the first tab, the ring is a faint 1px barely visible. omar-qa: Repro'd on NVDA+Firefox. SR announces "tab" but doesn't say which tab is selected. Tab IDs are clickable anchors without role=tab and aria-selected. kevin_m: Two issues then: visual focus not meeting contrast/weight; and semantics missing for tabs. For semantics we should use role="tablist" + role="tab" on each tab and set aria-selected on the active one, plus manage tabindex for roving focus. This helps SR users navigate. access-bot: scan results: MEDIUM: missing tablist/role semantics; MEDIUM: focus outline contrast and thickness insufficient (computed contrast < 3:1 for focus ring color #cbd5e1 on HC bg #000000). LOW: hover state color difference small for low-vision users. Recommend updating focus token and adding aria attributes. tasha-design: Proposed small pattern change: ```
``` Roving tabindex and keyboard handling for Left/Right arrows. Also we'll add a visible focus ring token for tabs: --focus-tab: 3px solid #00c2ff on dark / #005f99 on light. ben-frontend: Will implement role change and roving-tabindex. For focus ring, prefer a single token that adapts via color-modes: `--focus-tab: 3px solid var(--focus-accent)` and set `--focus-accent` per theme. Will add CSS fallback for high-contrast where UA colors override. omar-qa: QA checklist: 1) Tab to first tab, ensure focus visible and SR reads "Overview tab selected"; 2) Arrow keys move between tabs and SR reads the new tab name and selection; 3) When switching tabs, the active panel gets role=tabpanel and aria-labelledby to link back to the tab. Also test with NVDA/VO. kevin_m: Also ensure when a tab panel becomes active we don't push focus into the panel automatically. Focus should remain on the tab unless user presses Enter/Space to activate and move focus intentionally. That's standard WAI-ARIA Tabs pattern. tasha-design: UX question: should we include a visible selected underline in addition to aria-selected? Currently we only have the underline which is color-only. We need both: visual selected indicator and also an accessible name/state. ben-frontend: We'll keep underline but add aria-selected and update CSS so underline has a thicker 2px stroke and increased contrast. Also add an accessible transition that doesn't move focus during animation. access-bot: extra suggestion: include an aria-live=\"polite\" region to announce tab panel titles when changed via keyboard to help SR users who navigate content quickly. Not required if ARIA tabs implemented correctly, but helpful in some browsers. omar-qa: Add E2E: keyboard navigation across tabs + SR assertion: after arrow navigation, the screen reader output includes "tab" and "selected". We'll stub SR checks in Cypress with axe and a11y helper utilities. tasha-design: I'll draft the PR with markup changes, CSS token updates for --focus-accent, and a short test plan. @ben-frontend can you pick up the implementation? @omar-qa will add tests. ben-frontend: Taking the implementation. I'll keep change scoped and include unit tests for roving tabindex behavior and visual regression for focus styles. kevin_m: Quick UX micro-copy nit: aria-label for tablist should be "Model comparison" not generic "Tabs" so SR users get context. Also set title attr on hover. tasha-design: Good call. I'll put "Model comparison tabs" as aria-label. Thanks all :thumbsup:
